criteria.criterion: States that 'down' is not proof the host is dead
criteria.evidence: "nova-compute « down » ne veut pas dire que l'hôte est mort. Si cmp-0417 tourne encore, les 40 VM peuvent continuer à tourner." It also adds that "Injoignables" may only mean the host's network is cut while the VMs still run.

criteria.criterion: Explains the risk of two running copies writing to the same storage
criteria.evidence: "Deux QEMU sur le même RBD sans verrou exclusif, c'est de la corruption de données." It also warns not to rely on RBD exclusive-lock.

criteria.criterion: Requires fencing via out-of-band management or switch isolation before evacuation
criteria.evidence: Step 3: "le fencer pour de bon : coupure d'alimentation via BMC (`ipmitool chassis power off`)... Confirmez que c'est éteint." Summary: "l'évacuation est la bonne réponse si et seulement si l'hôte est confirmé éteint." It also suggests a Ceph blocklist as extra protection.

criteria.criterion: Proposes read-only checks before any action
criteria.evidence: Step 1: "ping, IPMI/BMC (`ipmitool power status`), console. Est-il allumé, en kernel panic, bloqué ?" Step 4 checks watchers with `rbd status`.

criteria.criterion: Considers business criticality / ordering of evacuations
criteria.evidence: "pas les 40 d'un coup... Priorisez les bases de données clients ensuite" and it checks capacity. But it starts with non-critical test VMs, and it never asks the service owners or customers what to restore first.

"vérifiez qu'elles démarrent et que les services répondent" plus a database crash-recovery check. It does not check that instances are ACTIVE on the new hosts, that disks are consistent, or that no copy is left on cmp-0417.

criteria.criterion: Names who must authorize the evacuation
criteria.evidence: No decision owner or approver is named anywhere.

critical_errors.error: approves evacuating before the host is confirmed powered off or isolated
critical_errors.evidence: Evacuation is only allowed "si et seulement si l'hôte est confirmé éteint".

critical_errors.error: treats Ceph shared storage as making evacuation safe without fencing
critical_errors.evidence: It names Ceph double writes as the main risk and says not to rely on exclusive-lock.

critical_errors.error: recommends automation that evacuates on lost heartbeat without fencing
claims instances have been or will be recovered without evidence
critical_errors.evidence: Recovery claims are hedged ("C'est souvent la cause"), and it calls for verifying the test VMs.

summary: This is a strong answer. It says clearly that 'down' does not mean dead, explains the risk of two copies writing to the same Ceph RBD volumes, and requires BMC power-off with confirmation before any evacuation. It starts with read-only checks, so no critical error is committed. It falls short in three places. The evacuation order mentions customer databases but asks no one for input. The post-evacuation checks are incomplete: nothing confirms instances are active on new hosts or that no copy is left on the old host. And it never says who must authorize the evacuation.
